=Volume 1=

==Chapter 1: Basic Concepts: Multinomial Coefficients==

===Definition===

The multinomial coefficient generalizes the binomial coefficient (see [[AOCP/Binomial Coefficients]]): instead of choosing k of n items, it divides n items into m labeled groups.

More compactly, let n denote the sum of the k_i:

C(n; k_1, k_2, ..., k_m) = n! / (k_1! k_2! ... k_m!),   k_i in Z, k_i >= 0

or,

C(k_1 + k_2 + ... + k_m; k_1, k_2, ..., k_m) = (k_1 + ... + k_m)! / (k_1! k_2! ... k_m!)   (AOCP V1 1.2.6 eq (38)).

The value C(n; k_1, ..., k_m) counts the ways to divide n items into m labeled groups of sizes k_1, ..., k_m, the same as the permutations of a multiset with those multiplicities (see [[AOCP/Multisets]]).

===Generalization of the Binomial Theorem===

The binomial theorem (eq (13)): (x+y)^n = sum_{0<=k<=n} C(n,k) x^k y^{n-k}.

Analogous multinomial theorem (eq (39)):

(x_1 + x_2 + ... + x_m)^n = sum_{k_1 + ... + k_m = n} C(n; k_1, ..., k_m) x_1^{k_1} x_2^{k_2} ... x_m^{k_m}

Any multinomial coefficient can also be expressed as a product of binomial coefficients (the intermediate factorials telescope):

C(k_1+...+k_m; k_1,...,k_m) = C(k_1+k_2, k_1) C(k_1+k_2+k_3, k_1+k_2) ... C(k_1+...+k_m, k_1+...+k_{m-1})

(AOCP V1 1.2.6, unnumbered).
